focus: Reinforcement-learning signal control trained in simulation
how this System differs: This System uses no learning of any kind: allocation is a deterministic function of measured density and queue length, so a decision can be explained from the frame it was made on. It is driven by junction video rather than a simulator.

focus: Density-only adaptive control from vehicle counts
how this System differs: This System adds tracked Queue_Length as a second measured term and weights the two with a tunable Alpha, which is the queue-aware extension under study; Alpha = 1 reproduces the density-only baseline exactly, so the comparison is measurable rather than asserted.

focus: A custom lightweight detector architecture for edge deployment
how this System differs: This System trains no detector and proposes no architecture: it consumes pretrained Ultralytics YOLO weights unchanged. No edge-hardware or latency claim is made; Processing_FPS is reported as measured on a desktop CPU or GPU.

focus: Graph-neural network traffic-state prediction across a network
how this System differs: This System predicts nothing and models a single isolated junction. Its control input is the current frame's measurement, not a forecast, and no network-level coordination is attempted.

This System's parameters are calibrated by hand against observed footage and recorded in config/default.json; the only sweep performed is over Alpha, reported per value, so each result stays traceable to the configuration that produced it.
